ObjectName.value: Carpet stretching arp

Categories.value: Taken with Olympus C-750UZ|PD-user|Yate, Gloucestershire|Fitted carpets|Carpet textile tools

ImageDescription.value:
Laying a carpet at a house in Yate, South Gloucestershire, England. 
The fitter is ramming his knee (with great force) on the black padded end of the tool. Spikes (unseen in the photo), on the lower surface of the other end of the tool, grip the carpet. The carpet stretches onto the spikes sticking up (again unseen) on the gripper strip that has been nailed down around the periphery of the room. The fitter simultaneously pushes the carpet edge down into the channel behind the gripper, using the chisel-like tool in his right hand, to produce a perfect edge.

ImageDescription.value:
Duke of Cornwall and York laying the foundation stone of St. John's Anglican Cathedral, Brisbane, 1901
A crowd of spectators gathered to see his Royal Highness, the Duke of Cornwall and York, lay the foundation stone of the Anglican Cathedral of St. John the Evangelist. A group of girls, wearing hats and dresses, can be seen standing in a circle in the centre of the crowd. For the Royal party a carpet has been spread through a lane leading to the Cathedral site, and a dais provided in front of the foundation-stone. Prominent persons are seated in the vicinity on a special square gallery erected on the site and decorated with red bunting and greenery.The Helidon pink stone, which forms the base of a choir pier, is suspended from the tripod in the middle of the enclosure. (Information taken from: The Brisbane courier, 22 May 1901).

ImageDescription.value: Vienna Hunting Carpet. Originating from the court of Shah Tahmasp I (r. 1524–76), the carpet’s design supposedly lay in the hands of the court painters. How the Vienna hunting carpet entered into the possession of the Austrian Imperial Court is still not exactly ascertainable. Its extraordinary quality suggests it was a diplomatic gift. Central Iran, probably Kashan, first half of the 16th century. Museum für angewandte Kunst, Vienna, T 8336
